mainTopic: Applying רבי אבא's rule of מחויב שבועה שאינו יכול לישבע to a single witness in a חזקה case
overview: A man grabbed a piece of metal from someone, and the case came before רבי אמי. One witness saw him grab it, and the man admits he grabbed it but claims it was his. רבי אמי asks how to rule: he can't be made to pay with only one witness, he can't be let off when there is a witness, and he can't swear because his own admission makes him like a גזלן. רבי אבא answers that he is מחויב שבועה שאינו יכול לישבע, and such a person pays. The rabbis studying before אביי wanted to use this rule for a single witness who says a possessor used a field for three years. אביי rejects that comparison. In the metal case the witness hurts the man, but in the field case the witness actually supports his חזקה. אביי concludes that רבי אבא's rule fits only one witness to two years of use, and only for paying back the produce.

steps.title: How should the judges rule in the snatched-metal case?
steps.stepSummary: רבי אמי, who was judging the case, lists three possible rulings for the man who admits snatching the metal, and shows that each one fails.
steps.simpleTranslation: How should judges decide this case? Make him pay? There aren't two witnesses! Let him go free? There is one witness! Have him swear? He himself said he snatched it, and since he said he snatched it, he is like a גזלן!
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אמי, who has to judge the case, is stuck. He goes through each normal ruling (pay, go free, swear) and shows why none of them works here.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Payment needs two witnesses, and there is only one. Going free ignores the one witness, and normally one witness forces the other side to swear. Swearing is blocked because he admits he grabbed the item, so he looks like a גזלן, and we don't trust a גזלן's oath.

keyTerms.meaning: One witness. Alone he cannot force payment, but he can force an oath.
Two witnesses, which is full proof
A robber. We don't let him swear to clear himself.

steps.confusionAlert: He is not admitting he stole. He admits he grabbed the item but claims it was really his. Because he took it by force with no proof it is his, he is treated like a גזלן.

phrases.english: How should judges judge this case?
Should he pay? There aren't two witnesses!
Should they let him go free? There is one witness!
Should he swear? But he said, "I did snatch it,"

phrases.aramaic: וְכֵיוָן דְּאָמַר דְּחַטְפַהּ – הָוֵה לֵיהּ כְּגַזְלָן!
phrases.english: and since he said that he snatched it, he is like a robber!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the case of the snatched metal, which the students want to compare to the single witness in the חזקה case.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which ruling applies when there is one witness, the person admits taking the item, and he cannot swear?

steps.title: רבי אבא: someone who must swear but can't, pays
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבא rules that the snatcher is מחויב שבועה שאינו יכול לישבע and so he must pay.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אבא said to them: He is someone who owes an oath but cannot swear, and anyone who owes an oath but cannot swear must pay.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אבא, who was sitting before רבי אמי, answers his question. Since the man is obligated to swear but can't, he has to pay.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The one witness creates a duty to swear. His own admission makes that oath impossible. Because he can't do what he is obligated to do, the claim against him stands and he loses the money.

keyTerms.meaning: The אמורא who gives the ruling
Someone obligated to take an oath

steps.whyThisMatters: מחויב שבועה שאינו יכול לישבע משלם is a major rule in דיני ממונות, and it comes up again and again across ש״ס.

phrases.aramaic: הָוֵי מְחוּיָּב שְׁבוּעָה שֶׁאֵינוֹ יָכוֹל לִישָּׁבַע,
phrases.english: He is one who is obligated to swear who is unable to swear,

phrases.aramaic: וְכׇל הַמְחוּיָּב שְׁבוּעָה שֶׁאֵינוֹ יָכוֹל לִישָּׁבַע – מְשַׁלֵּם.
phrases.english: and anyone who is obligated to swear but is unable to swear pays.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבי אמי's question from step 1.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: He pays, because he is מחויב שבועה שאינו יכול לישבע.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: כל המחויב שבועה שאינו יכול לישבע משלם.

steps.title: אביי: the two cases are not the same
steps.stepSummary: אביי rejects comparing רבי אבא's case to a single witness who says the possessor used the field for three years.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to them: Are they comparable? There, the witness comes to hurt him: if another witness joined him, we would take the item away from him. Here, the witness comes to help him: if another witness joined him, we would leave the field in his hands!
steps.whatsHappening: אביי pushes back on the students, who wanted to apply רבי אבא's rule to the three-years witness. He shows that the two witnesses work in opposite directions.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here is the test: imagine a second witness joined the first. In the metal case, two witnesses would take the item away, so the one witness is against the man and can force an oath. In the field case, two witnesses to three years would prove the man's חזקה, so the one witness is on his side and cannot obligate him to swear.

keyTerms.meaning: The אמורא who rejects the comparison
Are they comparable? A phrase that introduces a rejection.
To hurt or weaken someone's position
We establish or leave it (in his possession)

steps.confusionAlert: The one witness can only force an oath when he is testifying against the person. A witness who supports the person cannot obligate him in anything.

phrases.english: Abaye said to them: Are they comparable?!
There, the witness comes to weaken his position:

phrases.aramaic: כִּי אָתֵי אַחֲרִינָא בַּהֲדֵיהּ, מַפְּקִינַן לַהּ מִינֵּיהּ;
phrases.english: when another witness comes along with him, we take it away from him;
here, he comes to support him:
phrases.notes: "Here" means the witness who says the possessor used the field for three years.

phrases.aramaic: כִּי אֲתָא אַחֲרִינָא, מוֹקְמִינַן לַהּ בִּידֵיהּ!
phrases.english: when another comes, we leave it in his hands!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects using רבי אבא's ruling for the three-year חזקה witness.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the comparison only. רבי אבא's rule itself stays in place.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: In the field case the one witness supports the possessor rather than hurting him, so he cannot create an obligation to swear.

steps.title: Where רבי אבא's rule really fits: one witness, two years, for the produce
steps.stepSummary: אביי explains that רבי אבא's case matches one witness to two years of use, and only for paying back the produce.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, if רבי אבא's case is like anything, it is like one witness to two years, regarding the produce.
steps.whatsHappening: After rejecting the first comparison, אביי gives the correct one: a single witness who says the man used the field for only two years, where the question is whether he must pay for the fruit he ate.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Two years is not enough for a חזקה. So two witnesses to two years would make the man pay for the produce he ate, which means one witness is against him and obligates him to swear. He himself admits he used the field, so he can't swear to deny it. He is then מחויב שבועה שאינו יכול לישבע and pays for the produce.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather. It introduces the corrected version.
Two years, which is less than the three years needed for a חזקה
Produce, the fruit eaten from the field

steps.whatToRemember: A single witness only obligates an oath, and then payment under רבי אבא's rule, when he testifies against the person. In חזקה cases that means one witness to two years of use, and only for the produce, not for the field itself.

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא אִי דָּמְיָא הָא דְּרַבִּי אַבָּא –
phrases.english: Rather, if this case of Rabbi Abba is comparable to anything,
it is to one witness and to two years, and for the produce.
phrases.notes: He doesn't lose the field. He only pays for the fruit he ate.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא אִי דָּמְיָא הָא דְּרַבִּי אַבָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After rejecting the comparison in step 3, gives the case that really matches רבי אבא's rule.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: רבי אבא's rule applies to one witness who testifies to two years of use, obligating payment for the produce.
